text: Panning refers to the process of distributing a sound signal, whether originally monaural or stereophonic, into a new stereo or multi-channel sound field. This distribution is determined by a pan control setting. A common interface for this control is a pan pot, short for "panoramic potentiometer," which functions as an analog knob or slider. Physical recording consoles often feature these pan controls, typically positioned with a range from 8 o'clock (fully left) to 4 o'clock (fully right). In audio mixing software, virtual versions of these pan pots appear as on-screen knobs or sliders, providing the same functionality.
title: Panning (audio)

text: Panning is an audio technique employed in mixers to manipulate the stereo image. One specific application involves using panning to transform a stereo signal into a mono signal. This occurs when the left and right channels of a stereo source are panned centrally, meaning they are sent equally to both the left and right output channels of the mixer.
title: Panning (audio)

text: In a market economy, decisions concerning the production of goods and services are fundamentally guided by the interaction of supply and demand, establishing market prices. A key characteristic is that the allocation of resources for production is primarily determined by capital and financial markets. This contrasts sharply with planned economies, where state-controlled entities make investment and production choices.
title: Market economy

text: The mammalian sperm cell is structured with distinct parts: the head, neck, midpiece, and tail. The head encompasses the nucleus, which holds the densely coiled chromatin fibres, and is anteriorly covered by an acrosome containing enzymes for egg penetration. The neck section includes the sperm centriole. The midpiece features a central filamentous core encircled by numerous mitochondria, which are vital for generating ATP to power the sperm's journey through the female reproductive tract. The tail, or flagellum, is responsible for the lashing movements that drive the spermatocyte forward.
title: Sperm

text: Motile sperm cells, equipped with a single flagellum, propel forward uniquely and cannot swim backwards. Their movement towards an egg requires a water medium. Spermatozoa rely on mitochondria for energy, specifically those containing fructose within the seminal fluid. These mitochondria are situated in the midpiece, which is positioned at the base of the sperm head.
title: Sperm

text: An equilateral triangle is defined by having all three sides of equal length. This specific property contributes significantly to its symmetry. It possesses three distinct lines of reflection symmetry, meaning it can be folded onto itself along three different axes.
title: Equilateral triangle

text: Sharecropping is an agricultural arrangement where a farmer uses a portion of another person's land and gives a share of the produced crops to the landowner, keeping the remainder for themselves. This practice has a long history and exists in various forms across different cultures and agreements. Some systems are based on tradition, while others are formalized by law. Specific legal contract systems include the Italian mezzadria, the French métayage, the Spanish mediero, and the Islamic muqasat.
title: Sharecropping

text: Athens rose to prominence as the wealthiest Greek city-state around the late 6th century BCE. This ascent was significantly aided by the discovery of rich silver veins in the nearby mountains, which substantially increased their wealth. The city also developed an efficient trading network with other Greek states, focusing heavily on pottery, which constituted a large portion of their exports. Furthermore, Athens began importing grain because its own soil was not particularly fertile.
title: Economic history of Greece and the Greek world

text: The Canadian Prime Minister serves at Her Majesty's pleasure, meaning the post does not have a fixed term. Once appointed and sworn in by the governor general, the prime minister remains in office until he or she resigns, is dismissed, or dies. However, the term of a majority government is limited by an amendment to the Canada Elections Act, which came into effect in 2007. This amendment restricts the government's time in office to four years, setting the election day as the third Monday in October of the fourth calendar year following the previous polling date.
title: Prime Minister of Canada

text: A microscope slide is a fundamental component in preparing samples for observation. It is typically used in conjunction with a cover slip, a smaller glass sheet placed over the specimen on the slide. To position the slide correctly for viewing, it is placed **on the microscope's stage**. This placement allows for its secure holding, often achieved through specialized slide clips or clamps. In certain advanced or hygienic settings, a cross-table mechanism might be employed for precise, automated movement of the slide **on the microscope's stage**, ensuring accuracy without manual contact.
title: Microscope slide

text: The Articles of Confederation, formally the Articles of Confederation and Perpetual Union, served as the first constitution for the United States of America, establishing a loose alliance of the thirteen original states. Approved by the Second Continental Congress in 1777 and fully ratified by the states by 1781, it created a federal government intended only to possess the powers the colonies had previously granted to the king and parliament. A core principle of this agreement was to safeguard the independence and sovereignty of the states, meaning they retained the vast majority of governmental authority. Therefore, under the Articles of Confederation, the states held significantly more power than the central government.
title: Articles of Confederation

text: The history of Hawaii starts with human settlements sometime between 124 and 800 CE. Around 1200, Tahitians specifically arrived and initiated the settlement of the islands, laying the foundation for the Hawaiian civilization that followed. This initial arrival marked the beginning of a period of isolation lasting another 500 years.
title: History of Hawaii

text: Born on November 2, 1944, Michael Buffer is an American ring announcer known for boxing and professional wrestling. Buffer is also noted for his habit of rolling certain letters and adding inflections when pronouncing fighters' names. text: Product/market fit is a concept defined by Mark Andreessen. He stated that it occurs when a company is operating within a favorable market and has developed a product capable of fulfilling the needs of that market. Some interpretations also involve creating a minimum viable product to address existing problems or needs.
title: Product/market fit

text: Kidney transplantation is the surgical transfer of a healthy kidney from one person (the donor) to another (the recipient) suffering from end-stage renal disease. This procedure relies on organs sourced either from deceased donors or, crucially, from living-donor transplantation.
title: Kidney transplantation

It delves into contemporary social topics like sexuality, safe sex, promiscuity, and femininity, often contrasting friendships with romantic entanglements. title: Sex and the City

title: Golden State Warriors

text: Early in the twentieth century, specifically during its first half, John B. Watson established methodological behaviorism. His approach fundamentally rejected introspective methods, instead proposing that behavior should be studied solely through the measurement of observable actions and events. While Watson focused on the stimulus-response mechanisms seen in classical conditioning, notably those investigated by Ivan Pavlov, his work defined the initial phase of behaviorist thought. It was later, in the 1930s, that B. F. Skinner would introduce his own influential philosophy, radical behaviorism, which expanded the scope to include private events like thoughts and feelings.
title: Behaviorism

text: The idea of a North American Union, modeled after the European Union, has been discussed since the mid-19th century. This concept involves the potential integration of Canada, Mexico, and the United States. Following the implementation of NAFTA and the Maastricht Treaty, there was increased speculation about the possibility of forming such a union. While some proposals suggested a full-fledged union like the EU, others advocated for less extensive integration, such as a customs union or common market, among Canada, Mexico, and the US.
title: North American Union

text: The Ranjit Sagar Dam, also known as the Thein Dam, is a significant hydroelectric project located in the Indian state of Punjab. It was constructed by the Government of Punjab specifically on the Ravi River, a major waterway that forms a border between the states of India's Punjab and Jammu and Kashmir. Shah pur Kandi Township is the site for this dam, which is also situated near the cities of Pathankot and Kathua. Notably, 60% of the reservoir it forms is situated in Jammu and Kashmir. This facility represents the largest hydroelectric dam within Punjab. Development commenced with feasibility studies in 1953, followed by geotechnical investigations until 1980. Actual construction started in 1981, with the generators becoming operational in 2000 and the entire project completed by March 2001.
title: Ranjit Sagar Dam

text: In J. R. R. Tolkien's legendarium, the Undying Lands, a title sometimes used for Valinor, refer to the realm of the Valar located in Aman. While the name implies eternal life, the land itself did not grant immortality to mortals, though only non-immortals were permitted to reside there under specific circumstances. These exceptions included the surviving bearers of the One Ring—Bilbo and Frodo Baggins, and Samwise Gamgee—and possibly Gimli son of Glóin, who accompanied his friend Legolas to Valinor.
title: Valinor

text: The Undying Lands, once accessible to Men after the destruction of the Númenorean kingdom of Númenor, are now distant and veiled. However, for the Elves, these islands remain reachable only through a specific means: the ancient, straight road across the sea, and by utilizing ships that possess the unique power to sail beyond the normal confines of the world, past the spheres of the earth itself. Valinor, the blessed land on these islands, is the ultimate destination reserved for them.
title: Valinor

text: Felix Baumgartner, an Austrian skydiver and BASE jumper born on April 20, 1969, achieved significant fame for his jump from a helium balloon at high altitude on October 14, 2012. This event established world records for the highest skydive, estimated at 39 km, and the fastest recorded skydive speed, approximately 1,357.64 km/h or Mach 1.25. He notably became the first individual to break the sound barrier during a non-vehicular descent from the stratosphere. text: The Panzerarmee Afrika, led by Generalfeldmarschall Erwin Rommel, achieved a significant advance into Egypt by July 12th, 1942, following their victory at Gazala. Consequently, the British Eighth Army was forced to withdraw to a position near the coast, specifically within 80 kilometers of Alexandria, and the defense line was established around El Alamein. This location proved crucial as it was situated near the Qattara Depression, which restricted the front the Axis forces could exploit and prevented tanks from maneuvering into the area. The Axis advance was finally halted at this very point in early July, marking the start of the First Battle of El Alamein.

text: Beta decay represents a specific radioactive decay process where a nucleus emits a beta particle, either an electron or a positron, along with a neutrino. This transformation involves either converting a neutron into a proton and an electron (in beta-minus decay) or changing a proton into a neutron and a positron (in positron emission). The latter mechanism, positron emission, effectively turns a proton into a neutron within the nucleus. During beta decay, neither the beta particle nor its associated neutrino is present in the nucleus beforehand but is generated during the decay event. This process allows unstable atomic nuclei to achieve greater stability by adjusting their proton-to-neutron composition.

text: Basketball moves often involve specific offensive stances designed to create scoring opportunities. One fundamental position is the triple threat, which occurs when a player receives a pass while facing a defender and has not yet begun dribbling. In this stance, the player typically stands with their feet slightly wider than shoulder width, positioned lightly on the balls of their feet, and their knees gently bent. Their hands are usually resting on the ball or near their thigh, clearly demonstrating their capability to move in any direction. A single foot acts as the pivot point, while the other foot remains slightly forward. This setup is crucial because it allows the offensive player to immediately execute one of three primary actions: jump-shooting, dribbling past the defender, or passing the ball to a teammate. Mastering the triple threat effectively puts pressure on the defender, forcing them into a more reactive defensive posture.

text: An influential religion to enter China via the Silk Road during the Han Dynasty era was Buddhism. This faith appealed to Chinese intellectuals and elites, and its introduction was fostered through the development of gentry Buddhism, which offered an alternative to Confucianism and Daoism. The emphasis on morality and ritual resonated with Confucianists, while the desire for inner wisdom appealed to Daoists. Gentry Buddhism served as a medium for the religion's initial arrival and subsequently gained imperial and courtly support. By the early 5th century, Buddhism was firmly established in southern China. During this formative period, Indian monks continued to travel along the Silk Road to teach, and translation work was primarily carried out by these foreign monks.

title: Blond

text: The initial framework for the new government was set by James Madison's Virginia Plan, which was agreed upon by the delegates shortly after they began their deliberations at the Constitutional Convention. Other significant topics included the separation or consolidation of executive power, the eligibility and election of the chief executive (later termed President), the nature of impeachable offenses, the fugitive slave clause, the slave trade, and the appointment of judges. While these issues were highly contentious, the fundamental allocation of powers among the three branches was largely unchallenged. Following the early agreement on Madison's Virginia Plan, a Committee of Detail was formed to create a detailed draft, and later, a Committee on Style refined the language before the final document was approved and sent out.

text: After mating, the female red-eared slider often spends extra time basking to incubate her eggs. This period of waiting can last several days or weeks. Females possess the ability to lay multiple clutches within one year, with intervals between these clutches usually spanning twelve to thirty-six days. The actual fertilization of the eggs occurs during the laying process itself. Consequently, even if mating does not happen immediately following a clutch, the turtle can still produce fertile eggs later in the season because sperm remains viable inside her body. In the weeks leading up to laying, the female will often become less active in the water and exhibit behaviors like sniffing and scratching the ground, clearly indicating her search for a nesting site. Once found, she uses her hind legs to dig a hole specifically to deposit her eggs.
title: Red-eared slider

text: The arrival of the monsoons from the South Atlantic Ocean brings high humidity and heavy rainfall, which starts in central Nigeria typically in July and can be a daily occurrence throughout the following months, lasting till September before gradually beginning to retreat southward. These are the result of interactions between two dominant airmasses in Nigeria: the Maritime tropical air associated with the south westerlies and the Continental tropical air linked to the north easterlies. Rainfall amounts in central Nigeria vary significantly, ranging from 1,100 mm (43.3 inches) in the lowlands along the River Niger-Benue trough to over 2,000 mm (78.7 inches) along the southwestern escarpment of the Jos Plateau.

text: The Cyrus Cylinder, an ancient artifact, is widely recognized as being written by the Achaemenid king Cyrus the Great. This interpretation is based on traditional historical attribution. While some scholars debate the specifics of its content, its authorship remains attributed to Cyrus. Furthermore, the Cylinder was prominently displayed in Tehran by the Imperial State of Iran in 1971 as part of their celebrations marking 2,500 years of the Persian monarchy[15]. It also holds significance in modern times, as its sister, Princess Ashraf Pahlavi, presented a replica to United Nations Secretary General U Thant on October 14, asserting it represented "the heritage of human understanding, tolerance, courage, compassion and, above all, human liberty"[16]. This latter view, however, regarding it as the first declaration of universal human rights, has been contested by historians[8][9][10][11][12][13].

text: Human fertilization refers to the biological process where a human egg and sperm fuse. The dynamics of this process were identified by scientists during the nineteenth century.
title: Human fertilization

text: Human fertilization is the biological process where a sperm cell unites with an ovum. This typically occurs after ejaculation and ovulation. However, fertilization can also happen through methods like artificial insemination or in vitro fertilization, even without natural copulation or timing perfectly with ovulation. The sperm must penetrate the jelly coat surrounding the egg, a process enabled by enzymes released from its acrosome. Once inside, the sperm's plasma membrane fuses with the egg's plasma membrane. Following this union, the sperm head separates from its tail, and the fertilized egg, now called a zygote, begins its journey down the Fallopian tube towards the uterus.
title: Human fertilization

text: The development of rifling in firearms during the late 1500s revolutionized bullet manufacturing and accuracy. This process, which imparts a spin to the projectile, also creates unique marks on bullets corresponding to the specific barrel or mold used. Before widespread industrial production, these handcrafted barrels and molds were distinct, making comparisons possible. The crucial first documented application of this principle occurred in 1835, when investigators from London's Bow Street Metropolitan Police recovered a bullet from a murder scene. By matching its unique tool marks to a bullet mold found in a suspect's possession, they established the suspect's involvement in producing the projectile. This evidence, combined with other findings in the suspect's home, led to a conviction. However, as manufacturing shifted to standardized, mass-produced parts, the uniqueness of these marks diminished within a single company's output, making direct comparisons impossible. Experts noted that despite standardization, subtle microscopic differences would still exist between barrels due to manufacturing wear, and these distinguishing marks would be imparted onto each fired bullet.
title: Forensic firearm examination

text: The economic theory known as the "Strategy of Unbalanced Growth" is generally attributed to Albert O. Hirschman. He developed a comprehensive theoretical framework for this approach, which addresses the characteristics common in less-developed countries. These nations typically exhibit low levels of Gross National Income (GNI) per capita, alongside slow growth in this indicator. They also face large income disparities, widespread poverty, low productivity levels, significant dependence on agriculture, and a backward industrial structure. Furthermore, their economies often show a high proportion of consumption relative to savings, coupled with high population growth rates and dependency burdens. Unemployment and underemployment are prevalent, and there is typically technological backwardness alongside dualism, meaning both traditional and modern economic sectors coexist. Hirschman's theory contends that these features lead to resource scarcity or inadequate infrastructure, making it difficult to exploit available resources effectively. Consequently, the absence of sufficient investors and entrepreneurs prevents cash flows from being directed towards sectors that could influence balanced economic development.
title: Strategy of unbalanced growth

text: The concept of sustainability gained significant traction in policy and public discourse following the 1987 report by the United Nations World Commission on Environment and Development, known as the Brundtland Commission. This influential document, titled *Our Common Future*, introduced the widely accepted definition of sustainable development – development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. While the term itself might have existed prior, its formal integration into international development policy began with this landmark publication. This shift occurred alongside growing awareness of humanity's increased environmental footprint; over the preceding 45 years, global population growth and higher individual consumption levels had more than doubled the strain on Earth's resources. The evidence of sustainability efforts, such as recycling and renewable energy adoption, became more apparent in the latter part of the 20th century. The development of renewable energy technologies, including wind turbines, photovoltaics, and hydroelectricity, provided early sustainable alternatives to fossil fuels and nuclear power, with the first large-scale solar and wind power plants appearing during the 1980s and 1990s. Concurrently, local and state governments in developed nations started implementing sustainability policies on a smaller scale.
title: History of sustainability

text: Luke's Gospel and the Acts of the Apostles together form a two-volume work intended to address a specific theological question: how the Messiah of the Jews came to have an overwhelmingly non-Jewish church. text: The outermost layer of skin, known as the epidermis, contains no blood vessels or nerve supply. This layer is composed primarily of Merkel cells and keratinocytes, with melanocytes and Langerhans cells also present. The epidermis can be subdivided into several strata, beginning with the outermost: corneum, lucidum (found only in the palms of the hands and the soles of the feet), granulosum, spinosum, and basale. Cell formation occurs at the basale layer through mitosis. As these daughter cells move towards the surface, they undergo changes, die due to isolation from their blood source, and are replaced by new ones. The cytoplasm is shed, and the protein keratin is deposited, culminating in the shedding of the cells from the corneum layer – a process called keratinization. This keratinized epidermis acts as a vital barrier, preventing water loss and protecting against the entry of harmful substances and pathogens.
title: Human skin

text: External threats closely shaped the course of the Revolution. The Revolutionary Wars beginning in 1792 ultimately featured French victories that facilitated the conquest of the Italian Peninsula, the Low Countries and most territories west of the Rhine — achievements that had eluded previous French governments for centuries. Internally, popular agitation radicalised the Revolution significantly, culminating in the rise of Maximilien Robespierre and the Jacobins. The dictatorship imposed by the Committee of Public Safety during the Reign of Terror, from 1793 until 1794, established price controls on food and other items, abolished slavery in French colonies abroad, dechristianised society through the creation of a new calendar and the expulsion of religious figures, and secured the borders of the new republic from its enemies. Large numbers of civilians were executed by revolutionary tribunals during the Terror, with estimates ranging from 16,000 to 40,000. After the Thermidorian Reaction, an executive council known as the Directory assumed control of the French state in 1795. This period was marked by suspended elections, debt repudiations, financial instability, and significant military campaigns abroad, which elevated Napoleon Bonaparte to national prominence. However, the Directory faced persistent criticism, particularly concerning corruption, and eventually collapsed in 1799. The coup responsible for its downfall was orchestrated by Napoleon Bonaparte, who subsequently established the Consulate and later the First Empire.
title: French Revolution
